task_name: SlabVault - Collectible card marketplace image system
client_brief:
Consignment listing photographs where the holder and label remain legible

SlabVault handles graded collectibles. A listing photograph has to show the item and the evidence around it: holder, label and seal. Glare is a problem in the current set, but we cannot replace unreadable information with a convincing guess.

Please prepare
- Collectible listing tile: 14 named exports. The pictured card and visible holder label match this lot record. Source condition defects remain visible.
- Collectible condition-detail tile: 14 named exports. The grader, grade and certification number appear in the caption block. The photograph does not imply a different grade.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Graded with confidence, sold with proof
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019 in Providence, Rhode Island; a four person consignment house
brand_identity.about: SlabVault Cards is a small consignment house that lists and settles graded collectibles for private sellers. Lots run from roughly 150 to 5,000 dollars per item, and buyers decide from the photograph alone, zooming into the holder, the label and the corners before they bid. Consignors shoot their own slabs on their own tables, so the house exists to bring many different rooms to one credible standard. Trust is the entire product: everything SlabVault presents has to read as accurate, unretouched and verifiable.
brand_identity.audience: Condition-literate collectors aged 25 to 60 who buy graded cards and comics at 150 to 5,000 dollars a lot, read the grade and certification line straight out of the image, and walk away from anything that looks staged or concealed.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid to upper consignment. Not a bulk reseller or a toy shop, and not a fine-art auction room. The presentation sits deliberately between the two: neutral, generous and evidential, never cheap and flashy, never gilded and theatrical.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet, legible pairing: a humanist sans for body copy and roster data, and a slightly firmer grotesque or restrained slab for lot numbers and headings. Type stays small, even and confident. No decorative or display faces.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, factual, collector to collector. States the grade, the grader and the condition without hype. Never breathless, never salesy. The photograph does the persuading.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: SlabVault has never held a proper brand kit. What exists is a house note describing the palette in words (grey, black, one amber accent already used on the printed stationery and the sleeve ticket), the grading partner names spelled the way the graders require, and the sale details. There is no logo file, no type specimen and no template, so the house look has to be established fresh and held consistently across the listings, the printed tickets and the auction-week set.
brand_identity.values: Accuracy over polish. Show the item exactly as submitted, give every slab room to be read, and never add an edge, shine or shadow that was not there. The buyer's confidence is the asset the whole business protects.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
An obscured grading or compliance label must be rejected for reshoot, not reconstructed from guesswork.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.
